related_questions.question: How long does it take to show symptoms of Covid-19 after exposure?

text_blocks.snippet: If exposed to COVID-19, symptoms can appear anywhere from 2 to 14 days after exposure. The incubation period, which is the time between exposure and the onset of symptoms, varies for each individual. While some people may experience symptoms as early as 2 days post-exposure, others may not show any signs for up to two weeks. Monitoring for symptoms like fever, cough, and shortness of breath is recommended.

text_blocks.snippet: The time it takes to develop symptoms after exposure to an illness varies widely, ranging from a few hours to several weeks, depending on the specific illness. For example, the common cold can appear within 12 hours to 3 days, while measles can take up to 21 days. Some illnesses, like mononucleosis, can take several weeks to manifest symptoms.

COVID-19: Symptoms typically appear 2-14 days after exposure, with an average of 3-4 days for omicron and its subvariants.
Influenza (flu): Symptoms can appear 1-4 days after exposure.
Measles: Symptoms usually appear 8-12 days after exposure, but can take up to 21 days.
Mononucleosis: Symptoms can take 4-6 weeks to appear.
Strep throat: Symptoms can appear 2-5 days after exposure.
Chickenpox: Symptoms can take 10-21 days to appear.
Hand, foot and mouth disease: Symptoms can appear 3-6 days after exposure.
Pink eye (viral): Symptoms can appear 12 hours to 12 days after exposure.
Rubella: Symptoms can appear 12-23 days after exposure.
RSV: Symptoms can appear 4-6 days after exposure.
Tetanus: Symptoms can appear 3-21 days after exposure.
Walking pneumonia: Symptoms can take 2-4 weeks to appear.
